implemented: openviking/indexing/lexical.py: unified lexical provider with first-version local_fts5 (SQLite FTS5 BM25) backend; native provider explicitly rejected via provider_for() for non-certified deployments

Version-locked tokenizer (TOKENIZER_VERSION=zh-lexical-v1) applied identically to indexing and querying: CJK unigrams+bigrams, model-number preservation/expansion (SY215-C -> sy215-c, sy215, sy215c), DTC preservation (P0087), latin word tokens with -/_/ joins
encode_query() builds a conjunctive, per-token-quoted FTS5 MATCH expression; empty token streams are rejected instead of matching everything

FTS5 external-content index (lexical_rows + lexical_fts) with INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE triggers keeping the inverted index consistent with derived rows; only derived content is stored (content_sha for audit)
Index organised by account/namespace/document_id/index_generation with a scope index; LexicalIndex.generations() and drop() operate on that scope

Snapshot/authorization scoping resolved to rowids BEFORE ranking (scoped_rowids) for document_ids, index_generation, authorized_uris and content_kind; empty scope short-circuits to zero candidates rather than over-fetch-then-discard

Score direction normalized in the adapter layer: FTS5 bm25() lower-is-better is negated so higher is better; raw score retained in score_components.lexical_raw; score_normalized scaled to (0,1] by best-hit ratio; stable ordering by (score desc, rowid asc)
Portable BM25 fallback (okapi, k1=1.2 b=0.75) used only when SQLite lacks FTS5; FTS5 verified available in this environment

Index builds from child text (entries_from_chunks over chunk_fields-shaped records) AND image summaries (entries_from_image_records using the image.py 'summary' field), content_kind=text|image_summary

Generation-based publication participation: lexical_child_id()/lexical_receipt() produce a deterministic 'lexical:<sha256>' receipt child that callers can add to PublicationStore.begin(children=...) and acknowledge() only after the lexical write is durable
provider_for()/index_path() selection helpers; lexical index is an adapter component, not a second user-facing search API
